significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive coupling that query form changes the causal retrieval route and that a "small set of query-form-specific attention heads" predicts recall success, together with the form-(ii) claim that disabling those routers causes form-selective failures. This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—facts accessible under one query form but not another—and a mechanism separating form-invariant storage from form-dependent routing; it would constrain explanations across several query forms rather than merely show decodability, materially refining the MLP-enrichment/attention-extraction account used in Geva et al., "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models" (2023). Refutation would be moderately informative by ruling out the proposed compact-router explanation, although failure of this composite hypothesis would not by itself distinguish shared retrieval circuitry from distributed or content-dependent alternatives; true and false nevertheless denote distinguishable worlds. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic would support only the obvious hypothesis that retrieval varies with queries, not the specific router-head causal and predictive coupling, so the above-median score comes from the claim rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The claim names three usable handles: a "RetrievalDivergence score," router-head activation that "predicts per-example success," and a "form-transfer intervention" that injects an easy-form retrieval direction into a failing form. The activation predictor is ex ante relative to answer emission and the intervention provides an action window during inference, although both require access to model internals and the intervention additionally requires a successful alternative form of the same fact. After per-model re-extraction, the qualitative relation—greater form-specific routing failure and weaker router activation predict unsuccessful recall—would remain a prediction, while the identities of the heads and transfer directions would have to be rediscovered; the hypothesis is phrased across LLMs and multiple query-form classes rather than one dataset. Downstream users could build internal retrieval audits or inference-time repair systems, but the handles are not yet a model-agnostic deployment rule; deleting these specific handles leaves only the topic and would not justify this reach score, so the topic-substitution check passes.
